But even if the beer got hot enough to evaporate, it can't because it is covered by a layer of chicken fat! That's right, as the chicken cooks, fat and juices (myoglobin) drip into the can, and fat floats on top of the beer preventing any aromatics or moisture from escaping. You can see this in the pictures. The can actually weighs more after the cooking session because of the fat and myoglobin!

Check how fast a half glass of water evaporates if you put some cooking oil in it. Evaporation happens to open air and doesn't not occur through a layer of fat. If you don't heat the liquid enough to cause it to generate steam bubbles which can break through the oil, there is no evaporation. The beer can is acting as an insulator for the chicken because it prevents the hot air from the grill from ever reaching the inside of the chicken and it does not heat up quickly enough to transfer any meaningful amount of heat to the chicken.
